stem: If one die is rolled, then complete the activity to find the probability of the event that the number on the upper face is prime.
solution: \(S\) is the sample space. \(S = \{1, 2, 3, 4, 5, 6\}\), so \(n(S) = 6\). Event A: prime number on the upper face, \(A = \{2, 3, 5\}\), so \(n(A) = 3\). \(P(A) = \dfrac{n(A)}{n(S)} = \dfrac{3}{6} = \dfrac{1}{2}\).

If two coins are tossed simultaneously, find the probability of the event "getting at least one head."
solution: Sample space \(S = \{HH, HT, TH, TT\}\), so \(n(S) = 4\). Event A: at least one head, \(A = \{HH, HT, TH\}\), so \(n(A) = 3\). \(P(A) = \dfrac{n(A)}{n(S)} = \dfrac{3}{4}\).

stem: Solve the following simultaneous equations: \(x + y = 4\); \(2x - y = 2\).
solution: Adding the two equations: \((x + y) + (2x - y) = 4 + 2\), so \(3x = 6\) and \(x = 2\). Substituting in \(x + y = 4\): \(2 + y = 4\), so \(y = 2\). Solution: \(x = 2,\ y = 2\).
